text:
morgan: Heads-up — EU1 p99 spikes again during the 10:30 UTC traffic surge, network variance looks correlated. Seeing queue depth double for ~90s. Anyone on call?

arun: I'm on it, looking at egress across eu-cluster-a. Any recent routing changes?

morgan: No config changes. Traces show many requests getting routed cross-az during that window, latency to backend increases from ~12ms -> ~80ms.

jess: Can we throttle admission a bit for non-prod customers during the surge? We should buy headroom for p99.

laura: Throttle yes, but need numbers. What admit-rate delta buys us p99 from 450ms -> 250ms?

arun: Quick back-of-envelope: current steady qps=1.4k, avg service=60ms, p99 tail ~420ms. If we limit admitted qps to 1.1k with same batching, expected queueing contrib drops ~ (1.4/1.1 -1)*60ms ~ 21ms — not enough alone. Need 25-30% reduction or prewarm.

morgan: I ran a short sim locally: admission -20% + prewarm 40 GPUs reduces p99 to ~260ms for 10k-s interval. Tradeoff is ~620 GPU-hours for the 4-hour window.

jess: 620 GPU-hours is painful. Can we combine admission + KV-prefix cache hit boost to shave tokens?

laura: Cache helps per-token compute but not network tails. But if we increase cache hit from 45% -> 65% it cuts total token GPU time ~12% which reduces throughput pressure. Combo might hit target.

sre-rotation: infra-bot reports: ``net_eu1_packet_loss: 0.9% (10:28-10:32), cross-az latency variance +65ms``

arun: Packet loss that high explains TCP stalls -> amplified p99. Short-term fix: prefer intra-az routing for inference tier and increase TCP-retry backoff? Can we set route weight to avoid eu1-b during surge?

morgan: We can change routing policy but risk imbalance. Suggest gradual weighting: shift 15% away from eu1-b for 10 minutes, monitor queue depth.

jess: Also propose admission hysteresis: on p95>120ms OR packet_loss>0.5% trigger soft-admit -15%, then scale to -35% if p99 still >300ms after 30s.

laura: That hysteresis rule seems reasonable. Need to capture cost model: if hysteresis triggers for 2 hours/day at -35% we lose ~X revenue. We should quantify GPU-hours and cost.

arun: Quick calc snippet: ```
baseline_qps=1400
admit_drop=0.35
effective_qps=baseline_qps*(1-admit_drop)=910
gpu_capacity=64_gpus (each handles ~15 qps at target batch)
needed_gpus=ceil(effective_qps/15)=61
vs baseline 64 -> still within existing fleet but net revenue loss from denied requests ~490 qps-hours => approx 490*qps_hour_to_tokens*unit_price
```

morgan: Ops note: we prefer to avoid permanent fleet scale-up for transient network variance. Better to keep autoscaling but tighten admission edges.

jess: Agreed. Action items: 1) @arun toggle route-weight -15% away from eu1-b at 10:40 UTC and monitor for 10m, 2) @laura add hysteresis rule into admission controller playbook, 3) @morgan calculate precise GPU-hour cost and revenue impact for next FY forecast.

arun: On it. I'll post metrics after the shift (queue depth, p95/p99, packet_loss).

morgan: Thanks. If we still fail p99 after those steps, we fall back to emergency prewarm of 40 GPUs (pre-approve for 6h). :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deploy note — route weight change queued by arun; dry-run flag enabled.

jess: Thanks team. Please keep updates short.

arun: Update: route-weight change applied at 10:41 UTC. Initial 2m look — p95 improved from 135ms -> 112ms, p99 from 480ms -> 310ms, packet_loss down to 0.4%. Continuing to watch.

morgan: Nice. Save this thread for postmortem and capacity planning model. We'll bake new hysteresis into next-week SLO doc.

laura: I'll run forecast scenarios for winter surge assuming this kind of network variance — will share GPU-hour projections and a cost/benefit table.

arun: Posting the quick metrics snapshot: ``qps_before=1400 qps_after=1185 p95_before=135 p95_after=112 p99_before=480 p99_after=310 packet_loss_before=0.9% after=0.39%``

morgan: Perfect. Closing for now unless p99 creeps back. :white_check_mark:
